extracted.intended_audience: staff, volunteers, leadership, and member organizations of Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Washington (and parents/guardians)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and minimum safety standards for protecting youth at Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Washington, covering supervision, screening, training, reporting, technology use, transportation, facilities, emergency operations, and incident management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current safety membership requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All member organizations are required to adopt and adhere to safety policies that protect youth. Furthermore, all staff and volunteers must be trained on these policies annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership requires adoption of safety policies and annual training for staff and volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed approach to safety (National Council adoption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon adoption and annually thereafter, the National Council would review and approve minimum safety policies authored by CSQA for adoption by all Clubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These national minimum policies provide foundation but may be supplemented by Clubs with organization-specific operational details. Adoption of an entire Child & Club Safety Handbook is required under the proposed strategy to ensure core consistency, monitoring, and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-tolerance policy for child abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority of Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Washington is the physical and emotional safety of its members, staff, and volunteers. Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Washington maintains a zero-tolerance policy for child abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization implements policies and procedures for members, employees, volunteers, visitors or any victims of sexual abuse or misconduct to report any suspicion or allegation of abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-on-One Contact Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits isolated one-on-one interaction between Club participants and staff or volunteers, including board members. This includes prohibiting one-on-one contact at any time at the Club, in vehicles or by phone, text, social media or any other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions only for approved medical or counseling services by licensed professionals, and staff/volunteers (including minors) are strictly prohibited from meeting Club participants outside of Club-sponsored activities. The only other exception is if the Club participant is a child or sibling of the staff member/volunteer. Ensure all meetings and communications are never private; in-person meetings must be in areas where others are present or can see you; communicate to another staff member when an emergency exception arises; never transport one Club member alone; document any exceptions in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to one-on-one policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions may only be made when delivering approved medical or counseling services by a licensed, trained therapist or similar professional according to professional guidelines; when the emotional or physical safety of a member is at risk and Club leadership deems a private communication necessary; or in emergency situations that could create a safety risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exceptions are made, Clubs must disclose the meeting to Club leadership, regularly check in, place time limits, meet in rooms with clear sight lines, document the interaction, and if emergency, notify another staff member before engaging if practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of child abuse (including sexual abuse and physical assault)
rubrics_metrics.description: Child abuse is when an adult or another child, whether through action or by failing to act, causes serious emotional or physical harm to a child. Sexual abuse or misconduct may include any sexual activity with a minor, physical assault or sexual violence (rape, statutory rape, molestation), unwanted and intentional sexual physical conduct, and inappropriate activities, advances, comments, bullying, gestures, or electronic communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples including touching, pinching, patting, brushing, massaging, pulling against another’s clothes, and electronic communications; enumerates conduct types that may constitute abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grooming — definition and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Grooming is when someone builds an emotional connection with a child to gain their trust for the purposes of sexual abuse, sexual exploitation, or trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grooming behaviors may include targeting specific youth for special attention, isolating youth from family/friends, one-on-one interactions such as sleepovers or camping, gradually crossing physical boundaries (full-frontal hugs, lap sitting), and other boundary-crossing behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated reporting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Every staff member or volunteer who becomes aware of or has suspicion of child abuse or neglect must immediately report to Club leadership. Club leadership is responsible for reporting the incident immediately to the appropriate authorities according to statewide mandated reporting laws, as well as to Boys & Girls Clubs of America (BGCA) within 24 hours via the critical incident system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate reporting to leadership and external authorities; BGCA notification within 24 hours via critical incident reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training (types and intervals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before providing services to young people, and annually thereafter: BGCA-approved child abuse prevention, BGCA-approved mandated reporting, BGCA-approved grooming prevention. Annually: all the policies, including all safety policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required for all staff and volunteers with direct repetitive contact with young people and must be conducted and reported through a BGCA-approved process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical interactions — appropriate vs inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff and volunteers are required to maintain appropriate physical contact with minors. Examples of appropriate: side hugs, handshakes, high-fives, holding hands with young children in escorting situations. Examples of inappropriate: full-frontal hugs or kisses, lap sitting, wrestling or piggyback/shoulder rides, tickling, allowing youth to cling to an adult’s leg, showing affection in isolated area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists illustrative behaviors; staff must avoid listed inappropriate behaviors and adhere to appropriate touch practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbal interactions — appropriate vs inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff and volunteers must maintain appropriate verbal interactions. Appropriate examples include positive reinforcement, child-appropriate jokes, encouragement, praise. Inappropriate examples include name calling, inappropriate (adult-only) jokes, discussing sexual encounters or personal issues, secrets, profanity or derogatory remarks, harsh language that may frighten or humiliate youth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative lists; inappropriate verbal interactions can lead to disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse and safety resources (visibility and parent notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCGW prominently displays BGCA-approved collateral that shares ethics hotline, crisis textline and safety helpline information with members, staff, volunteers, and families. All safety policies are shared with parents and guardians upon receiving a youth membership application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep resources visible and provide policy access to parents/guardians at membership intake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of private vs public contact/communication
rubrics_metrics.description: One-on-one interaction is any private contact or communication (including electronic) between any Club participant and an adult. Private contact/communication is any communication in person or virtual between one youth and one adult that is secluded, not in plain sight and/or done without the knowledge of others. Public contact/communication involves at least three individuals (e.g., two staff and one member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of private: meeting behind closed doors, transporting one member alone, one-on-one electronic communications. Examples of public: meetings in plain sight, group electronic communications, transporting multiple members or public transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring program guidance under one-on-one prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentorship is important; prohibition of one-on-one interaction does not have to negatively affect mentoring. Mentors should hold sessions in areas where other staff/members are present or visible, copy parents/staff on communications when appropriate, schedule meetings during Club hours at the Club, and document interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on adjusting mentoring practices to comply with one-on-one rules and document interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: External mentors and partnership requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All local mentors are required to abide by Club policies, including background check requirements and prohibition of one-on-one interaction. External mentors must abide by all Club safety policies and have a written agreement defining custody/responsibility transfer for members; procedures should be communicated to parents/guardians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require written agreements, documentation of interactions, and adherence to screening and supervision rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision requirements (continuous sight/sound and staffing)
rubrics_metrics.description: All Club activities and program spaces shall always be under continuous supervision by sight or sound (for restroom supervision) by an appropriate adult staff (18 or over).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff and volunteers must abide by one-on-one prohibition, disciplinary policies, ensure at least one adult (18+) is present when supervising members, maintain proper supervision ratios, be trained on supervision tactics, ensure youth staff/volunteers are supervised by adult staff, and immediately notify leadership and submit written reports for supervision issues, accidents, or critical incidents. Prohibits use of electronic devices while supervising unless for Club purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restroom usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be either a designated adult restroom or procedures to ensure adults and minors never utilize a restroom at the same time. Clubs will either have single-user restrooms or multi-user restrooms with single stalls that can be secured from the inside. On field trips, a minimum of three youth will be escorted by one staff member who will wait outside the main entrance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design or procedures to prevent adults and minors using restrooms simultaneously; require single-stall options or specific escorting rules on trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restroom monitoring and incident handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrooms shall be regularly monitored by designated staff according to a schedule set by Club leadership. Monitoring includes walk-throughs and inspections and best practices such as limiting number of children in restrooms, prohibiting younger children and teens from sharing a restroom, positioning staff near restroom entries for auditory supervision, and designing multi-user restrooms to eliminate outer doors while maintaining stall privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff observing unacceptable restroom conditions must notify leadership immediately, document incidents in writing, and report per Incident Reporting Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrance and exit control
rubrics_metrics.description: All facility entries and exits shall be controlled and monitored by paid adult staff (18 or over) during all hours of operation, along with a system to monitor and track everyone who is in the facility. All exit doors shall have an audible alarm. Only designated adult staff shall be authorized to possess keys/badges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an employee supervises an activity they are responsible for security of program space; maintain tracking systems and alarms to discourage unauthorized use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility condition and access control
rubrics_metrics.description: All program spaces shall have clear lines of visibility and be monitored by adult staff when in use. Areas not in use shall remain locked and accessible only by adult staff. Interior/exterior spaces must be well-lit, clean, free of hazards; storage closets and unused spaces locked during operational hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damages posing imminent risk must be repaired immediately; leadership should consider temporary/permanent closure if immediate repair not possible. Report critical-incident-level damage to appropriate authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food and drink safety compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any distribution, preparation, or consumption of food/drink must comply with applicable food services sanitation and public health codes. If food is prepared onsite, required health department inspection certificates must be posted; dangerous kitchen utensils must be securely stored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow local health codes and post certificates when required; secure dangerous utensils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background checks (scope, timing, and disqualifying findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal background checks of all employees (including minors), board volunteers, and all volunteers who have direct repetitive contact with minors. Checks may be name- or fingerprint-based and shall at minimum: verify identity and legal aliases (SSN), provide a national Sex Offender Registry search, provide a comprehensive national criminal search and a comprehensive local criminal search (statewide or county), and include any additional criteria required by policies/funding/licensing or jurisdiction (e.g., motor vehicle records, child abuse registry, credit checks). Checks must be conducted prior to employment and at intervals not to exceed 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All findings considered in hiring/volunteering decisions. Disqualifying factors include refusal to consent, false statements, registered sex offender status, convictions for listed felonies (murder, child abuse, domestic violence, abduction/human trafficking, rape/sexual assault, arson, weapons, assault/battery, recent drug convictions within 5 years) and convictions for misdemeanors/felonies against children including child pornography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing — behavioral-based requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In-person behavioral-based interviews will be conducted with every candidate for employment or volunteer service. BGCA will provide behavioral-based interview questions for local use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use behavioral interviewing to assess candidate suitability for working with youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference checks are conducted on any candidate with direct repetitive contact with young people. If candidate has prior Boys & Girls Club experience, obtain information on eligibility for rehire/volunteering from previous Clubs before extending an offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reference materials when requested by other Member Organizations; consider references in hiring decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff and volunteer onboarding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon offer, new employees receive and confirm in writing receipt of an up-to-date employee policies and procedures manual/handbook that includes conditions of employment, benefits, rights/responsibilities, Club safety policies, and other employment-related information. Before working with members, staff/volunteers receive orientation covering mission/goals/policies, job descriptions/performance standards, participant needs, personnel policies, operational policies related to safety and completion of required Child Abuse Prevention trainings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document receipt of handbook; orientation must precede work with members and include completion of required BGCA-approved training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug- and alcohol-free workplace policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees are prohibited from reporting to work or working while under the influence of alcohol and/or illegal or unauthorized drugs. Unlawful or improper use of drugs presents a danger; organization must comply with Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must notify supervisor of criminal drug/alcohol violations; violations may result in disciplinary action up to discharge. Organization may inspect lockers/personal property when reasonable suspicion exists and take lawful enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoking policy
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCGW will comply with applicable regulations regarding non-smoking. Smoking (including tobacco, e-cigarettes, vaporizers) is prohibited at all properties except external areas where specifically authorized. Policy applies to employees, volunteers, and members while on Club premises or during Club activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrict smoking to designated external areas only; comply with federal/state/local rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable suspicion indicators and response
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff/volunteers must notify leadership of behavior suggesting influence of drugs/alcohol. Leadership will determine whether the employee should be examined/tested per drug-testing policies. Employees believed to be under the influence will be required to leave premises; illegal drugs will be turned over to law enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of behavior: odors, unsteady movements, eye symptoms, flushed face, slurred speech, emotional changes, actions (yawning, twitching), absences around weekends/holidays, repeated accidents, damage to inventory. Use these indicators to trigger evaluation and testing as permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and testing rights and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization reserves the right to inspect organization-issued lockers, desks, or other suspected concealment areas and an employee’s personal property when reasonable suspicion exists. Screening, testing and security measures may be used as methods of enforcement as permitted by state law. Refusal to submit to testing is a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests paid for by organization are property of organization; exam records treated as confidential in separate medical files but may be shared as required by law or with authorized persons/insurance/doctor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription medication and legal drugs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees/volunteers are prohibited from reporting to work when using legal drugs except when use is pursuant to doctor’s orders and doctor advises substance does not adversely affect ability to perform duties. Those taking legal drugs that could affect safety must notify supervisor so job performance/reasonable accommodation can be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An employee may be prevented from performing duties until determination/accommodation is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reporting — definitions and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear reporting procedures are required for incidents that might occur in Clubhouses. Safety incidents include inappropriate adult-youth activity, inappropriate youth-youth activity, allegations of abuse, bullying, inappropriate electronic communications, medical emergencies, accidents, threats, assaults, missing children, criminal activity, and other incidents as deemed appropriate by leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety incidents include occurrences during Club programs, on premises, and during Club-affiliated trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal incident reporting — required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any employee/volunteer who becomes aware of an incident shall immediately complete an incident report and submit it to Club leadership. Incident Report must include date and location, incident details, witnesses/contact info, names of all involved, and all notifications made (first responders, parents, leadership, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and submit reports immediately; document all relevant details and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: External incident reporting and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCGW follows all mandated reporting statutes/regulations and applicable federal/state/local laws. Types of incidents reported externally include inappropriate adult-youth activity, inappropriate youth-youth activity, allegations of child abuse, child pornography, criminal activity, and missing children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with external mandated reporting and licensing requirements; ensure prompt notification to appropriate authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident investigation procedures and interim actions
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCGW supports external investigations and internal investigations by the Safety Committee when not externally reportable. Federal/state/local criminal and mandated child abuse reporting laws must be complied with before internal investigations. Internal investigations are not a substitute for criminal or child protective services investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incident involves allegation against staff/volunteer/member, suspend that individual immediately (employees with pay) and maintain suspension throughout investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: BGCA critical incident reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Member Organization shall immediately report any allegation of abuse or potential criminal matter to law enforcement and report critical incidents to BGCA within 24 hours. Critical incidents include: any instance/allegation of child abuse by staff/volunteer (current or former); youth-on-youth sexual misconduct; child abduction/missing from site; major medical emergency leading to extended hospitalization/permanent injury/death; incidents involving staff/volunteer misconduct; failure to comply with childcare licensing requirements; felony-level crimes on site; misappropriation of funds ($10,000+ or any federal funds); criminal/civil legal actions involving the organization; negative media attention that could compromise reputation; any other incident deemed critical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to report to BGCA could result in funding hold or provisional status. Report to law enforcement immediately where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Acceptable Use — member usage (signing and authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using Club technology or personal device at Club, both member and parent/guardian must read and sign Technology Acceptable Use policy. Club devices and personally owned devices defined; Club purposes defined (program activities, career development, communication, homework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized use only during approved times and locations; prohibition on device use in locker rooms, restrooms, and areas with expectation of privacy; members expected to ask staff if unsure about permissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Acceptable Use — member prohibited uses, monitoring, internet access, and discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Members may not use technology to harass, threaten, demean, humiliate, intimidate, embarrass, or annoy peers/others. Club reserves right to monitor/inspect personally owned devices (parents notified beforehand and may be present); failure to allow inspection may bar future device use. Members are responsible for device security and Club not liable for loss/damage. Inappropriate use can result in confiscation, suspension, termination of membership or referral to law enforcement. Internet access must be via Club’s filtered wireless network; Club can manage/close access to sites. Digital citizenship rules mirror Code of Conduct. Members must complete BGCA digital citizenship and technology safety training annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists examples of inappropriate communications (obscene/profane/sexual/threatening language, personal attacks, harassment, defamatory information, communications promoting destruction/criminal acts); monitoring procedures and parental notification; training requirement for device use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Acceptable Use — staff and volunteer usage and communication restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must read and sign Technology Acceptable Use policy before using Club or personal devices. Club devices/personal devices defined; Club Purposes include program delivery, sanctioned training, communication for Club purposes. Staff may not use technology to harass/threaten/demean; inappropriate use can lead to disciplinary action including termination. Staff may never use personal devices to communicate directly with a single Club member — communications must include an additional staff member and at least two Club members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization reserves right to monitor/inspect personally owned devices; staff refusing inspection may face disciplinary action up to termination. Provide examples of cyberbullying; prohibit direct one-on-one electronic communications with members including overnight events. Staff must follow internet access procedures (use filtered network) and secure devices with strong passwords; list and enforce disallowed apps/sites where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology security: password, access, scanning and disallowed apps
rubrics_metrics.description: Devices must lock themselves and require authentication using strongest features available; a minimum standard would require a typed password of at least six characters or numbers. Disallowed apps/websites should be listed by organization where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require authentication, recommend biometrics where available, maintain list of disallowed apps/sites during work hours, and enforce access controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation policy — scope and general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCGW only provides transportation to/from Clubhouse and approved off-site locations using Club vehicles or other vehicles approved by Club leadership. The Club only transports youth in Club vehicles or vehicles approved by leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not transport members in personal vehicles; maintain logs of transported youth; ensure drivers cleared by DMV/background checks; ensure at least three individuals present when transporting (two adults and one member or one adult and two members); never use cell phones while transporting; document transportation incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation — driver requirements and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Drivers must allow DMV background check and be cleared per barrier crime policy, keep updated lists of transported youth, confirm no children left on vehicles (seat-by-seat scan and daily log), perform regular checks to ensure pickups/drops occur at appropriate times/locations, submit written reports for transportation issues, only transport members in official Club vehicles, ensure at least three individuals present when transporting, never transport members in personal vehicles, never use phones while driving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce driver screening, documentation, vehicle-use rules, and reporting of transportation incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehicle safety and equipment standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency vehicle should meet local/state/federal inspection and licensing requirements. Inspect vehicles before trips; perform regular maintenance and keep records. Vehicles must provide seat belts for every passenger, have a complete first-aid kit, working/current fire extinguisher, reflective warning signs, be clean and well maintained, and repair exterior damage promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DMV and state requirements; maintain inspection/maintenance logs and safety equipment on-board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared-use restrooms on trips — 'rule of three' and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: On field trips or using public restrooms, youth shall never enter alone unless single-stall and empty. Use the 'rule of three'—at least two youth plus an adult walk to restrooms and three youth enter multi-stall facility together. Adult remains outside for auditory surveillance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should monitor and clear restrooms before use, hold doors partially open at doorway if appropriate, or position near sinks if doorway position is not feasible. Use practices like shutting exterior restroom door and using 'Occupied' sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accident or emergency transportation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Driver should immediately notify Club leadership if there is a delay or issue (e.g., breakdown, accident, emergency) with transporting members. Staff shall immediately inform leadership if a staff/volunteer/board member violates transportation policy; organization will take disciplinary action up to termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify leadership promptly, follow emergency procedures, report incidents in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Operations Plan (EOP) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs shall create and maintain an EOP that at minimum encompasses mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery for emergencies such as fire, severe weather, lockdown, bomb threat, suspicious package; includes training/drill schedule and reporting procedures and be developed/shared with local first responders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EOP must be maintained, shared with first responders, include training/drills, and cover mitigation/preparedness/response/recovery steps including accommodations for persons with disabilities/special needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOP annual review and safety committee oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Club leadership will maintain a board-led safety committee that regularly focuses on safety and will have oversight and responsibility for the EOP. The safety committee is responsible for reviewing and updating the EOP annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual EOP review by board-led safety committee; maintain governance oversight for emergency planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Aid and CPR training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCGW always maintains a minimum of one CPR- or first-aid-trained staff on site during all operating hours when members are being served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure trained personnel are on-site at all operating hours; maintain training records and scheduling to meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key emergency definitions and preparedness concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided for Emergency (events that place life or significant Club assets in danger), Mitigation (efforts to reduce loss of life/property), and Preparedness (actions that help everyone act quickly and decisively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions as the basis for planning: mitigation actions should be taken before emergencies; preparedness should include evacuation strategies for those with disabilities or special needs and keep stakeholders informed.
